tldr: October's papers framed continual learning around forgetting, replay selection and agent benchmarks. November turned to cheaper adapters: RASP (Nov 2) keeps a single fixed-size LoRA instead of one branch per session, and a Nov 9 paper shares one prompt across tasks with no rehearsal data.
whats_new: Nov 18: two papers move continual learning toward deployment, one adding specialist vision models to a trained multimodal agent's tool space, the other (Hypnos) running continual learning end to end on edge devices.
why_it_matters: Updating a deployed model or agent without retraining or regressions is the cost problem here; fixed-size adapters and incremental tool addition are the mechanisms that would make it cheap.

status.detail: Four arXiv papers in November; all research-stage, none shipped in a product or framework.

beats.headline: Fixed-cost adapters replace per-task growth
beats.summary: Two vision-transformer papers bound parameter cost: one stationary-size LoRA, then one shared prompt with no replay buffer.

beats.headline: Continual learning reaches agent tool spaces and edge hardware
beats.summary: Incremental tool addition for multimodal agents and an end-to-end edge platform, both on Nov 18.

open_questions: Does the tool-space extension paper show that adding a specialist model leaves existing tool-use accuracy unchanged?
Do RASP or the single-prompt method report results beyond vision transformers, on LLMs?
Does Hypnos release code or report on-device memory and latency figures?
Do any of these methods report results on the Continual Learning Exam benchmark from October?
take_for_builders: Do not adopt yet; if you add tools or fine-tune adapters on a live agent, rerun the old task evals after each update to catch regressions.
